CA.name: California
CA.law_name: California Consumer Privacy Act, as amended by CPRA; DELETE Act
CA.citation_range: Cal. Civ. Code 1798.100 et seq.; DELETE Act at 1798.99.80 et seq.

appeal.note: CCPA has no statutory appeal step. Escalate directly to the CPPA or the AG.

ag_complaint.name: California Privacy Protection Agency
ag_complaint.note: CalPrivacy enforces the data broker registry and DROP.

CA.thresholds: Businesses with >$25M gross revenue, or buying/selling/sharing personal info of 100k+ consumers/households, or deriving 50%+ of revenue from selling/sharing personal info.

preferred_mechanism.name: Delete Request and Opt-out Platform
preferred_mechanism.residency_verification: California residency verified via the California Identity Gateway (Socure / Login.gov).
preferred_mechanism.penalty: $200 per request per day of noncompliance
preferred_mechanism.note: A single verified request binds every registered data broker. For a California resident this supersedes per-broker outreach entirely. Do not automate submission: the DROP Terms of Use prohibit exploiting access to the platform, and it is a one-time manual step regardless.

OR.name: Oregon

appeal.note: On denial of an appeal the controller must tell the consumer how to complain to the Attorney General.

ag_complaint.name: Oregon Department of Justice, Privacy Unit
ag_complaint.note: The Attorney General has sole enforcement authority. In the first year the Privacy Unit received 214 complaints, a majority concerning online data brokers.

broker_registry.note: Registration is required before collecting, selling or licensing brokered personal data in Oregon. A verification tool exists but no bulk download. An unregistered broker is already in violation, which is useful leverage in a complaint.

OR.thresholds: Controls or processes personal data of 100,000+ consumers, OR 25,000+ consumers while deriving over 25% of annual gross revenue from selling personal data.

cure_period.note: The 30-day right to cure sunset on 2026-01-01. The AG may now enforce immediately.

TX.name: Texas
TX.law_name: Texas Data Privacy and Security Act

appeal.note: Appeal response is 60 days, not 45. On denial the controller must provide a method to complain to the Attorney General.

ag_complaint.name: Office of the Texas Attorney General, Consumer Protection
ag_complaint.note: Complaints are filed through the online form.

TX.thresholds: Applies to entities doing business in Texas that process personal data, excluding small businesses as defined by the SBA. Notably broader than the consumer-count thresholds used by most states.

VA.name: Virginia

appeal.note: Citation and appeal window need primary-source confirmation.

ag_complaint.name: Virginia Office of the Attorney General

VA.thresholds: 100,000+ consumers, OR 25,000+ consumers while deriving over 50% of gross revenue from the sale of personal data.

CO.name: Colorado
CO.thresholds: 100,000+ consumers, OR 25,000+ consumers while deriving revenue from the sale of personal data.

CT.name: Connecticut

ag_complaint.name: Connecticut Office of the Attorney General

CT.thresholds: 100,000+ consumers, OR 25,000+ consumers while deriving over 25% of gross revenue from the sale of personal data.
